questions: Does the upstream fix compose with the Phase 209 hermetic fixture, or is it shadowed by it?
Do all git-invoking tests inherit the env layer, or do some construct env from scratch?
Can this host verify the fix at all, given its git version?

findings.evidence: git >= 2.5x runs 'git maintenance run --auto --detach' after commit/merge; it daemonizes and repack -d keeps deleting loose objects and shard dirs after the foreground call returns
auto-maintenance is a built-in default, not a configured behavior, so pinning GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM cannot disable it; upstream tried the same approach and it failed

findings.item: env-config layer composes with Phase 209 pinning
findings.evidence: with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM pinned to a nonexistent path plus GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0, 'git config --get maintenance.auto' returns 'false' rc0; without the layer it is unset rc1
scratch_env() builds from {**os.environ}; 14 test files shell out to git and every env dict derives from os.environ, including the two that build their own
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_KEY appear nowhere in tests/ or qor/

findings.item: this host cannot validate the fix's effect
findings.evidence: GH #308 correlates the behavior with git version and names 2.52 immune vs CI 2.54.0; the obvious pack-count regression test would pass vacuously here
pyproject packages include = ['qor*']; tests are not shipped, so nothing consumer-visible changes

brief_path: GH #308 (upstream root-cause analysis adopted as the research artifact)
